title: Historical EEO/AA training for RTEC managers and supervisors
summary: Historical manager/supervisor training packet emphasizing nondiscrimination, fair and documented selection, reasonable accommodation, recruitment outreach, staff development, termination review, complaint prevention, EEO/AA accountability, and management responsibility. The packet also includes adapted external/reference content that must not be mistaken for RTEC-specific policy.

claims.claim: The training instructs managers and supervisors to communicate nondiscrimination expectations, maintain EEO/AA records, support reasonable accommodations, promote staff development, and act promptly on sexual-harassment allegations.
The training describes a fair-selection model using job-related criteria, consistent reference checking, written records, reasonable accommodation, and documentation of the full selection process.

The packet describes manager responsibility for analyzing personnel actions for differential impacts and reviewing selection, pay, promotion, reclassification, layoff, discipline, training, and termination for bias.

The packet repeats a historical RTEC hiring workflow in which HR obtains CEO approval to advertise/interview, recruits through newspaper/OET, conducts interviews, routes selected driver candidates for background screening, obtains CEO final selection, and then schedules DOT physical/drug screening before indoctrination/training.

evidence.page_or_section: About Staff EEO Compliance / Employment practices

steps: Review EEO/AA responsibilities and nondiscrimination expectations.
Apply fair recruitment and selection practices.
Recognize and respond to harassment/discrimination concerns.
Review personnel actions for differential impact or bias.
Use EEO/HR resources for review and escalation.
outputs: Manager/supervisor EEO awareness and documented personnel practices
controls: Source repeatedly emphasizes job-related criteria and consistent treatment.
Source emphasizes documentation of interviews, reference checks, personnel decisions and terminations.
Externally adapted training excerpts are not promoted as RTEC-specific policy without corroboration.
